newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC sees DRAM prices stabilising this year--paper.
newsitem.headline: NEC sees DRAM prices stabilising this year--paper.

text.p: NEC Corp believes prices of dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips will stabilise this year, a Japanese business daily said on Monday.
NEC vice president Hajime Sasaki made the comments on DRAM chip prices in an interview with the Nihon Keizai Shimbun.
He also said that a full-fledged shift to 64-megabit DRAMs from 16-megabit DRAMs would occur in the middle of 1998, the paper said.
Sasaki said global demand for DRAM chips in value terms would show a double-digit increase in 1997 against a seven percent fall last year, the newspaper said.

Japanese semiconductor makers are expected to invest a total of about 750 billion yen in semiconductor-producing plants and equipment in the year from April 1, 1997 but they might revise up their plans in the middle of the business year, the paper quoted Sasaki as saying.
"Prices will not fall further and they will stabilise this year," Sasaki told the newspaper, referring to DRAM chip prices.
Sasaki was also quoted as saying Japanese chip makers" total capital investment in their semiconductor business was expected to be 815 billion yen for 1996/97.
NEC is planning to make capital investment of 190 billion yen in its group"s semiconductor business in 1997/98, unchanged from its investment in 1996/97, Sasaki said.

Sasaki said spot prices of 16 megabit DRAMs had sharply recovered over the last few weeks to $8 following news that South Korean makers would cut output. He was quoted as saying he did not know whether the Koreans" production cut was a temporary move or not.
